title: Coefficient-linear trace with prescribed geometric degree
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with identity, let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite étale morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $G$ be a sheaf of $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] on the small étale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $d\in\mathbf N$ and suppose that for every separably closed field $\Omega$ and every $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$, the set of lifts of $s$ to $Y$, namely the geometric fibre [def-weil-pbc-geometric-fibre], has cardinality $d$. With inverse image, direct image and the unit $\eta_G:G\to f_*f^*G$ as in [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image], there exists an $R$-linear sheaf morphism $t:f_*f^*G\to G$ such that $t\circ\eta_G=(d\cdot1_R)\operatorname{id}_G$. No invertibility of $d\cdot1_R$ is assumed.

source.place: Section 03SH (section-trace-method), Definition 03SE (definition-trace-map), its localization and sum characterization and the following restriction/trace degree formula; local splitting: Etale Morphisms Lemma 04HN

proof.text: For each point of X, choose an étale neighbourhood on which f is a finite coproduct of copies of the neighbourhood, using finite étale local splitting. A separably closed geometric point of a nonempty neighbourhood identifies the summands with the lifts counted by the geometric fibre. Hence the splitting has d summands. The resulting neighbourhoods cover X.

Use the étale inverse-image restriction isomorphism and the direct-image split-cover product description to identify f_*f^*G locally with the product of the copies of G. Restriction is the diagonal. Take the sum of the coordinate projections: it is R-linear since restriction maps are R-linear. The construction is natural in the site object.

Forget coefficients on each splitting neighbourhood. Under the étale restriction isomorphism these additive sums are exactly the split sum formula of the unique abelian trace family. Its étale-localization property identifies their restrictions on overlaps, so the underlying additive maps agree; faithfulness of forgetting modules proves equality of the coefficient-linear maps. Pull the splitting cover back to every site object and glue the local maps with the sheaf condition. Uniqueness of gluing proves coefficient-linearity and naturality, giving t : f_*f^*G → G.

On every splitting neighbourhood, restriction followed by the sum sends s to d copies of s added together, i.e. (d : R) • s. Sheaf separatedness checks the equality on this cover, proving η_G ≫ t = (d : R) • id_G. The empty sum is zero, covering d = 0 as well.
